title: A young person's seva
hookLine: the first seva a young person chooses
tomorrow: an amrit sign-up sheet. how would Simran know she's ready?

cards: At a big Sunday gathering, the gurdwara's coordinator holds up a clipboard: who wants a job? Rotis, dishes, the water line, the shoe racks. Last week the adults handed Fateh a pitcher.
This week nobody hands him anything. He's been told he can pick. Simran expects the kitchen, where the action is.
Instead Fateh walks straight to the shoe racks by the door, where an old man is setting out pairs, and asks if he can help.

teach.b: Seva is selfless service, and the Granth puts it right in the middle of ordinary life.
On ang 26, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: serve here, in the midst of the world, and you'll be given a seat of honor in the Lord's court. Not away from the world. In it, at the door, with the shoes.
Children in langar are handed jobs.
The first seva a young person chooses is different: nobody assigned it, so it's theirs. Fateh says he picked the shoes because the old man looked like he could use a friend. Good company again.
And Simran makes her choice the same night. She writes back to the camp director: yes, one week, move-in or not.
Two first choices in one family. Now the last six days come back in one breath. Honest answers: nobody knows that, and here's what I do know.
Their own sikhi, by keeping and by asking. Calm courage: frighten no one, fear no one. Learning together.

how: Young Sikhs may begin seva at the gurdwara with jobs handed to them, then choose their own: the kitchen, the dishes, the water line, or the shoe racks by the door.

games.q: what does “a young person's seva” mean?
o: the volunteer hours a school asks a student to log
the service an elder assigns at the dastar bandi
the first service a young Sikh chooses for themselves

games.q: the last six days — tap the pairs.
p: nobody knows that; here's what I know
frighten no one, fear no one

s: from this week: in Japji, Guru Nanak says the pandits and qazis know when the world was made
pauri 21 says they didn't find it; only the Creator knows.
on ang 26, Guru Nanak says to serve in the midst of the world
and you'll be given a seat of honor in the Lord's court.
Kabir's sandalwood salok tells you to choose your neighbors carefully
from yesterday: the trees near the sandalwood become fragrant. good company changes the company.

games.q: a teen at your community center is told she can pick any volunteer job. she picks the least glamorous one. going by today, what do you say?
o: steer her toward something that'll look better on applications.
nothing; volunteering only counts when an adult assigns it.
let it be hers. a first choice of service belongs to the one who made it.
games.why: Fateh chose the shoe racks, and nobody steered him. the first seva a young person chooses is theirs.

practice: Look at your own hands, palms up, for a full minute. Remember the jobs they've been handed, and of one they might choose: something small that no one would ask of you. Then let them rest and sit with that choice.

wordCard.voice: A young person's seva. The first service a young Sikh chooses, instead of being handed.

carryVoice: The first seva: nobody assigned it, so it belongs to the one who chose it. Two weeks, done.

sources.ref: Ang 26 (Sri Rag, Guru Nanak: vich duniaa sev kamaaeeai taa dargeh baisan paaeeai), paraphrased
